newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Mig 1996 net seen within expectations.
newsitem.headline: San Mig 1996 net seen within expectations.

text.p: Philippine food and drink giant San Miguel Corp said on Wednesday its 1996 net income from operations dropped by two percent but stock analysts said it was within expectations.
"There were no surprises. The figures were generally within expectations," said Jonas Ferrer, vice president for research at Pryce Securities.
Analysts said they expected the beer-based conglomerate to either report weaker or flat earnings this year, and a modest recovery in 1997.
SMC reported a net income of 6.09 billion pesos in 1996, up four percent from 5.84 billion in the previous year.

But the 1996 figure was bolstered by extraordinary gains coming from the sale of certain assets and a second-quarter write-back of 561 million pesos of provisions made in previous years, it said in a statement.
Excluding extraordinary gains, San Miguel's 1996 net income declined by two percent to 5.26 billion pesos from 5.38 billion in 1995, or to 2.57 pesos per share from 2.63, the company said.
